column1: # Partition table for DOOM on ESP32-S3-RLCD-4.2 (16MB flash)
# Offsets are explicit rather than blank-and-auto so that the WAD partition's
# address is stable: it is baked into the flashing command
# silently would flash the WAD into the wrong place.
# Alignment rules that constrain this layout:
#   - app partitions must start on a 64KB (0x10000) boundary
#   - data partitions must start on a 4KB (0x1000) boundary
#   - the table itself lives at 0x8000 and occupies 0x1000
# The WAD partition is additionally 64KB-aligned on purpose: the ESP32-S3 MMU
# maps flash in 64KB pages
column2: so an aligned partition maps without a partial

column1: # leading page.
# Type 0x42 / subtype 0x06 is the WAD. ESP-IDF reserves partition types
# 0x00-0x3F for itself and leaves 0x40-0xFE to the application.
# WAD partition sizing -- 5M
#   shareware DOOM1.WAD = 4
#   4 MiB partition     = 4
# The stock shareware WAD overflows a 4MiB partition by 1
# worked around this by shipping a cut-down 3.1MB WAD; we would rather hold the
# unmodified file. 5M is the next size up that keeps the following partition
# 64KB-aligned.
# Note this only covers shareware. Ultimate Doom (~12MB) and Doom II (~14MB) do
# not fit in 16MB flash alongside a 3MB app -- those need the SD card.
# Flash the WAD with:
#   esptool.py -p <port> write_flash 0x310000 doom1.wad
